source_facts.fact: Current NPPF defines Green Belt purposes and the grey-belt concept; Green Belt policy aims to keep land permanently open and prevent urban sprawl.
source_facts.gate: Grey-belt identification does not automatically allocate land, release it from Green Belt or grant permission.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data reports 190 Green Belt records; collector last ran 23 July 2026 and warns the annual-return snapshot may not reflect later boundary changes.
source_facts.gate: Service geometry is a time-stamped planning dataset, not a current legal boundary determination for a parcel.

source_facts.fact: The statutory duty applies to National Parks, the Broads and National Landscapes; National Landscape is the non-statutory rebrand of AONB.
source_facts.gate: Designation creates duties and planning considerations, not automatic refusal or approval.

source_facts.fact: The national framework covers 44 Protected Landscapes and states its targets are non-statutory shared ambitions.
source_facts.gate: National targets cannot be converted into parcel obligations or scores without applicable policy and site evidence.

source_facts.fact: Grades 1, 2 and 3a are Best and Most Versatile; detailed post-1988 surveys and strategic/provisional maps have different scales and evidential uses.
source_facts.gate: Strategic ALC mapping cannot replace a site-specific survey where detailed classification is needed.

source_facts.fact: Planning guidance requires consultation with Natural England for certain non-agricultural proposals causing loss of more than 20 hectares of BMV land outside a development plan.
source_facts.gate: The consultation trigger is not an automatic planning refusal and requires proposal-specific facts.

core_rules: Green Belt designation is not an automatic refusal of development
grey-belt identification is not automatic allocation or planning permission
grey-belt land remains subject to the full applicable NPPF decision framework
Green Belt openness is a planning concept and not a parcel development score
Green Belt service geometry must retain its snapshot date
annual Green Belt returns can lag later local-plan boundary changes
Planning Data Green Belt origin warnings must be preserved
absence from a service snapshot does not prove absence from current Green Belt
Green Belt purpose assessment requires policy evidence and cannot be inferred from proximity alone
previously developed land in Green Belt is not automatically developable
Golden Rules apply only where the relevant policy circumstances are met
release from Green Belt through plan-making is distinct from application approval
Protected Landscape designation is not automatic refusal
National Park administrative boundary is not a planning decision
National Landscape is the non-statutory name for AONB and the legal designation must remain clear
Protected Landscapes duty applies to relevant authority functions and is not a parcel score
management-plan objectives are not individual development permissions
Protected Landscapes targets are non-statutory shared ambitions
national protected-landscape targets must not be downscaled to a parcel
setting effects can extend outside a Protected Landscape boundary
absence of polygon intersection does not prove no effect on landscape setting
landscape significance requires proposal-specific assessment
AONB service data must retain authoritative-source and update metadata
National Park service data must not be substituted for the governing authority decision
Agricultural Land Classification is land-quality evidence not planning permission
BMV comprises Grades 1 2 and 3a and must not include Grade 3b
provisional ALC at strategic scale is not a detailed site survey
predictive ALC at strategic scale is not a measured parcel classification
post-1988 detailed survey polygons must be matched to the actual site before use
historic ALC surveys can pre-date current site conditions and boundaries
Grade 3 must not be assumed to be 3a or 3b without suitable evidence
Natural England consultation trigger is not automatic refusal
20 hectare BMV consultation threshold depends on proposal and plan context
loss of agricultural land is distinct from soil handling and construction impacts
soil quality cannot be inferred solely from ALC grade
agricultural capability does not determine housing viability
strategic map confidence does not equal parcel-level accuracy
Planning Data ALC origin warning must be preserved
Natural England open-data availability does not make every dataset site-survey quality
national planning policy must be applied with the development plan and material considerations
consultation guidance is not a consent decision
dataset collector date is not designation or survey date
current web publication does not make historic survey observations current
policy rebranding must not change statutory designation semantics
screening evidence must remain separate from candidate promotion
NO_DATA must not be converted into no Green Belt or landscape constraint
no parcel relation allocation permission or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel accuracy
